notes: The parts are unchanged from step 1, and every part is in the catalogue.
The manual's circuit text says 'Analog input 2', but the images and the rest of the text use A0. I used A0.

Photoresistor divider, as in the image: 5V rail to the photoresistor (column 6), photoresistor to column 10, 10k resistor from column 10 to column 13, then to the ground rail. A0 is on column 10, the junction.

LED branch, as in the image: pin 9 goes by blue wire to the LED anode (column 22). The LED cathode is in column 23. The 220 ohm resistor runs from column 23 to column 26, then by black wire to the ground rail. The resistor therefore sits on the cathode side, as the breadboard image shows. The schematic draws it on the pin 9 side. The two are electrically equivalent in series.

The catalogue's breadboard naming puts rows a-e in the top bank 't', whereas the image labels the top half f-j. I used bank 't' for the whole build area, and only the column strip matters. The rail holes (tp = top plus, tn = top minus) are numbered approximately by image column.
The Arduino GND wire goes to the second GND pin on the power header (GND.2), as the image shows.
